newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bel-20 index set to notch up more gains.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bel-20 index set to notch up more gains.

text.p: The Bel-20 index, consolidating in light volume on Wednesday after a series of five firmer sessions, was heading for fresh gains which could propel them to record levels next week, traders said.
"Next week we might attack the previous highs," said Stefan Casteleyn at Corluy & Co. The Bel-20, which ended 0.13 percent lower at 1,753.31, set a life high of 1,781.63 in May.

Dealers said the market would be jittery ahead of the release on Friday of U.S. August CPI. "Inflation data, on Friday 13th, there is bound to be some speculation and we could see a volatile day," one trader said.
But most expected the Bel-20 to clear Friday's hurdle without any stumbling, drawing their confidence from the light volume which accompanied today's dip.
"We've been going up on heavy volumes and today we slipped on light volume, that's a very good sign," Casteleyn said.
Dealers also said that first-half company earnings so far had been mostly positive and would help underpin the market.
Generale Bank, which announced a lower-than-expected 8.6 percent rise in first-half group net profit on Tuesday, was a notable exception, slipping 1.3 percent to 11,175 francs.
Dealers said they had been anxiously awaiting results of electronics firm Barco, which has been one of the few market favourites in recent months but closed unchanged at 5,410.
"Hopefully Barco will not let us down," said Casteleyn shortly before the company announced a 37 percent jump in consolidated net profit to 1.13 billion francs.
Potential investors in steel wire and cord maker Bekaert also clearly held their breath before earnings news.
Bekaert, which closed unchanged at 23,200, later announced first-half group net profit fell 25 percent to 1.27 billion.
